newsitem.title: USA: Quaker State restructures into 8 divisions.
newsitem.headline: Quaker State restructures into 8 divisions.

text.p: Quaker State Corp. said Thursday it was restructuring its diverse automobile products businesses into eight units.

The restructuring will leave each division focusing on a specific product group or geographic region, including motor oil manufacturing, Q Lube fast-lube locations, automotive appearances units and air freshener units, the company said.
Quaker said it has developed units for its Canadian operations and Blue Coral International, which sells commercial car wash products in Britain, Australia and Singapore.

Sheldon Adelman resigned Wednesday as vice chairman and chief executive officer of the Irving, Texas-based company's consumer products division and will serve as a consultant instead until 2001, Quaker added.
Quaker also said it will buy 1.4 million shares of its stock from Adelman at $16 a share, a price agreed to on Nov. 20. Adelman's stock options were also redeemed for a lump sum, the company said.
Adelman will continue to hold 750,000 shares that he received in the acquisition of Blue Coral, Quaker said.

Quaker said the shares purchased from Adelman will not affect the company's previously announced plan to repurchase up to two million shares of its stock in the open market or in negotiated transactions.
Quaker is principally a producer of motor oil and lubricants, both branded and private label, and a marketer of products and services in the automotive aftermarket.
Quaker's stock fell 37.5 cents to $15.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
